title: Save a sheath's weapons with a pet and extract them with the sheath
description:
Closes #17

Phase 5 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p5` (`bfaaa8799`): two code commits, each with its test, a test
commit, and the plan's record of the phase.

## Cause

A sheath's weapons hang off `sheath_primary` and `sheath_secondary`, and nothing else holds
them. Only the player save (`player_save_objs_sheathed`, rows under the owner's name) and the
`sheath` / `unsheath` commands handled them.

- `objsave_save_obj_record_db_pet()` wrote no sheath rows, and a pet has no rows under an
  owner's name anyway: a loaded sheath given to a pet came back empty when the pet was restored,
  and its weapons were in no row.
- `extract_obj()` did not look at them: junking or selling a loaded sheath, and the extraction
  after a rent save, freed the sheath and left the weapons in `object_list` with no holder.
  After a rent save their rows were written, so that was a leak only; after a junk or a sale
  they were gone from play without having been destroyed.

## What changes

`59bc44f45`: `extract_obj()` extracts what a sheath holds, beside the loop that extracts a
container's contents. Nothing nulls the pointers afterwards: the sheath is freed in the same
call. `Test_object_extraction_takes_a_sheaths_weapons` (no database) extracts a sheath holding
two weapons and finds `object_list` as it was; without the change the two weapons stay.

`2b8959cdd`: `Crash_save_pet()` writes a sheath's weapons as the pet's own objects beside the
sheath, through the pet record writer, as `House_save()` does for a house: no new table and no
migration. A worn sheath's weapons are written at `MIN(0, location)`, as inventory records,
since `pet_object_graph_valid()` refuses two records on one wear position and with them the
whole set; a carried sheath's are written at its own depth, so a sheath in a bag puts its
weapons in the bag. The restored pet carries the weapons and an empty sheath.
`Test_pet_save_stores_a_sheaths_weapons_as_its_own` (database) saves a pet with a worn sheath
holding a blade and a shield and a carried sheath holding a dagger through `pet_save_objs()`
and loads it through `pet_load_objs()`: five rows, one of them with a wear position, and the
restored pet wears an empty sheath and carries the other sheath, empty, and the three weapons.
Without the change the save writes two rows.

`4a9bd579b`: the pet test also refuses a weapon's row, the blade's and then the shield's; each
attempt fails the save, as any refused row does, and leaves the records written before it. The
first matrix run had left those two failure lines uncovered.

`docs/systems/SAVE_SYSTEMS_BREAKDOWN.md` has the pet rule, in the pets section.

The plan's check before the change held, with nothing to change: `overwrite_object()` keeps a
target's own sheath pointers (phase 7), every writer's temporary object comes from
`read_object()` or `create_obj()`, and the editors free their copies with
`free_object_strings()`, never `extract_obj()`.

## Found while building

The leak #17 describes never showed in the memory-check or sanitizer jobs, and could not have:
a weapon left behind stays on its rnum hash chain, so valgrind and LeakSanitizer count it as
still reachable. `Test_house_save_stores_a_sheaths_weapons_as_its_own` is clean under valgrind
with and without the fix; it no longer extracts its weapons by hand, since the teardown's
extraction of the sheath takes them. The extraction test watches `object_list` instead.

## Verification

- Both new tests fail on the code of `0b88bb81d`: the extraction test with the two weapons still in
  `object_list`, the pet test with 2 rows written instead of 5.
- The two new tests, the house sheath test and the refused-row save test are clean under
  valgrind, with the database on.
- `make -j16 test` on `4a9bd579b`: 2055 tests pass. `make install` done.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, on a database freshly built from `sql/master_schema.sql`:
  2055 of 2055 pass.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master` on `2b8959cdd`: 33 of 33 jobs pass
  (522 s); the unit, sanitizer and memory-check jobs run 2055 tests each. The persistence changed
  lines were 4 of 6 covered, above the floor, the two uncovered being the refusals `4a9bd579b`
  then covered.
- On `4a9bd579b`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (256 s); the unit, sanitizer and memory-check jobs run 2055
  tests each, and the persistence changed lines are 100% covered.
- The format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on `bfaaa8799`, which adds the plan's record
  only.

## Not in this merge request

- The player sheath loader's debug trace (`SHEATH1` to `SHEATH6`, and the text of its
  `SELECT`) logged at every load: work item #33, seen while building and not changed here.
  `objs_from_sheath()`, which had no caller, went in the review round (below).
- `otransform`'s copy of a fresh object over the live one, which leaves the live object on its
  old rnum hash chain with the fresh copy's links and miscounts both prototypes: work item #34,
  pre-existing, seen while fixing the review findings.
- A sheath's weapons are not walked by `Crash_extract_norents()`: a rentable sheath keeps a
  no-rent weapon through a rent, as before.
- No deploy: the fixes reach production with the next release.

## Review round

Three findings, fixed one commit each after the tag; the plan's phase 5 section has the record.

| Thread | Commit | Test |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Stale sheath slot read through freed memory | `079e9bd6e` | `Test_gameplay_sheathed_weapon_extracted_alone_leaves_its_slot`, `Test_player_load_puts_a_sheaths_weapons_back_in_it`, `TestArmCountUnsheathChecksEachItem` |
| A sheathed artifact's destruction invisible to the ledger | `8a8f0fdd7` | `Test_artifact_integration_sheathed_instance_destruction_releases_ownership` |
| `delete_object()` destroys a deleted sheath's weapons and walks into one freed | `da68e251a` | `Test_gameplay_object_delete_hands_a_sheaths_weapons_to_its_wearer` |

A sheathed object now knows its sheath (`sheathed_in`); `obj_to_sheath()` and `obj_from_sheath()`
in `src/core/handler.c` set and clear the slot and the back-pointer together, at every site.
`extract_obj()` takes a sheathed object out of its sheath as it takes an object out of a room,
a character or a container; `artifact_on_extract()` counts a sheathed object as placed; and
`delete_object()` hands a deleted sheath's weapons to its holder beside the contents.

Verification, on `da68e251a`: the first gameplay test fails on `bfaaa8799` with the reviewer's
valgrind read at `handler.c:3098`; the artifact and delete tests fail on `079e9bd6e` with only
their test applied, the delete one with the walk reading the freed dagger under valgrind. The
sheath, artifact and renumber tests are clean under valgrind with the database on; `make -j16
test` passes 2059 tests; `./cutest` with the database tests on, on a fresh
`sql/master_schema.sql` database, passes 2059 of 2059; the local matrix: 33 of 33 jobs pass (1431 s); the unit, sanitizer and memory-check jobs run 2059
tests each, the persistence changed lines are 100% covered and the olc changed lines 75%, both
above their floors, and the clang-tidy gate has no finding. The
format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on the record commit.
